title: Thailand floats the baht
entity: Bank of Thailand; Government of Thailand
summary: On 2 July 1997, Thailand abandoned its exchange-rate peg and allowed the baht to float after mounting pressure on its currency and foreign-exchange reserves. The move became the opening trigger in the Asian financial crisis, which spread through several economies in the region.
why: The episode exposed vulnerabilities linked to short-term foreign borrowing, currency mismatches, weak financial-sector balance sheets and pressure on fixed exchange-rate regimes. Thailand entered an IMF-supported adjustment programme in August 1997. The crisis then affected Indonesia, Korea and other regional markets, although each country experienced its own sequence of events.
impact: The downturn brought recession, financial-sector restructuring and significant social strain across affected economies. The IMF's retrospective account reports that Thailand's real GDP fell by more than 10% in 1998. This record describes the regional crisis trigger; it does not imply that every later consequence occurred in Bangkok itself.

sources.label: IMF — Financial Sector Crisis and Restructuring: Lessons from Asia
IMF — Thailand: Public Information Notice and crisis chronology

title: Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy
entity: Lehman Brothers
summary: Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on 15 September 2008. The failure of the investment bank became one of the defining moments of the global financial crisis and intensified already severe stress in credit and funding markets.
why: Lehman's collapse was not the sole cause of the global financial crisis. It was a major escalation within a crisis rooted in housing-market losses, securitisation, leverage and fragile short-term funding. Its failure disrupted counterparties and confidence across interconnected financial markets.
impact: The crisis contributed to a deep global recession, rising unemployment, business failures, foreclosures and household financial distress. The scale and timing of impacts differed across countries. This card does not attribute individual deaths to the bankruptcy; such claims require separate, carefully sourced evidence.

sources.label: Federal Reserve History — The Collapse of Lehman Brothers
U.S. Bankruptcy Court — Lehman Brothers case information

title: India announces withdrawal of ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes
entity: Government of India; Reserve Bank of India
summary: On the evening of 8 November 2016, the Government of India announced that existing ₹500 and ₹1,000 banknotes would cease to be legal tender from midnight, subject to specified exceptions and exchange/deposit arrangements. The RBI's annual report records that these notes represented nearly 86% of the value of currency in circulation on 8 November 2016.
why: The policy was presented by the government as a measure against counterfeit currency, illicit wealth and corruption, among other stated objectives. Its implementation required rapid cash exchange, deposits, new-note distribution and changes to withdrawal arrangements.
impact: The sudden withdrawal of high-denomination cash disrupted cash-dependent transactions and required households, firms and banks to adjust. The intensity of effects varied by region, occupation and access to banking and digital payments. The RBI later documented the remonetisation process and the volume of notes supplied. This record does not claim a uniform impact across every Indian state or city.

sources.label: RBI Annual Report 2016–17 — Currency Management
RBI Circular, 9 November 2016 — Withdrawal of legal tender character
RBI FAQ — Specified Bank Notes

title: WHO characterises COVID-19 as a pandemic
entity: World Health Organization
summary: On 11 March 2020, the World Health Organization assessed that COVID-19 could be characterised as a pandemic. The public-health emergency rapidly became a global economic shock as restrictions, voluntary distancing and uncertainty affected production, travel, employment and demand.
why: Financial markets repriced sharply during the early pandemic period. Governments and central banks introduced emergency fiscal, monetary and liquidity measures. The shock was unusual because it combined a public-health crisis with supply disruptions and a sudden fall in demand.
impact: The economic and human consequences varied widely across countries and communities. Job disruption, business closures, income losses and unequal access to support were widely documented. This event is pinned to Geneva as the location of the WHO announcement; its effects were global, not confined to Switzerland.

sources.label: WHO — Director-General's remarks, 11 March 2020
WHO — COVID-19 timeline
IMF — World Economic Outlook, April 2020

title: Silicon Valley Bank is closed by regulators
entity: Silicon Valley Bank; Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
summary: On 10 March 2023, California banking authorities closed Silicon Valley Bank and appointed the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation as receiver. The FDIC reported that the bank had approximately $209 billion in total assets and $175.4 billion in deposits at 31 December 2022.
why: The failure followed a rapid loss of depositor confidence and liquidity pressure. The bank's customer base was concentrated in technology and venture-capital-related businesses, and a large share of deposits exceeded the standard insurance limit.
impact: The failure raised concerns about deposit flight and vulnerabilities at other regional banks. On 12 March, U.S. authorities announced steps to protect all depositors of the former SVB under a systemic-risk exception. Shareholders and certain unsecured debt holders were not protected.

sources.label: FDIC — SVB closure and receivership, 10 March 2023

title: RBI cuts the policy repo rate to 6.25%
entity: Reserve Bank of India; Monetary Policy Committee
summary: On 7 February 2025, the Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee reduced the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 6.25%, with immediate effect. It retained a neutral monetary-policy stance.
why: The decision was made after the MPC assessed the evolving macroeconomic situation. A repo-rate change influences the policy rate corridor and can affect market interest rates, borrowing costs and monetary transmission, although the pass-through to individual borrowers is neither immediate nor identical.
impact: The decision applied to India's monetary-policy framework nationally. Mumbai is shown because it is the RBI's headquarters and the institutional location associated with the policy record; the economic effects were not limited to Mumbai.

sources.label: RBI — Monetary Policy Statement, 7 February 2025
RBI — Governor's Statement, 7 February 2025

title: Trump administration announces a new reciprocal tariff framework
entity: The White House; U.S. Government
summary: On 2 April 2025, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14257 establishing a new U.S. reciprocal tariff framework. The order set a 10% baseline additional tariff on imports, with higher country-specific rates announced for selected trading partners.
why: The measure marked a major shift in U.S. trade policy and prompted responses from trading partners, businesses and financial markets. The policy and its subsequent modifications evolved over time, so this record identifies the initial framework rather than treating every later tariff rate as unchanged.
impact: The order was issued in Washington, D.C., but applied to imports entering the United States and affected trade relationships worldwide.

title: RBI keeps the policy repo rate at 5.50%
entity: Reserve Bank of India; Monetary Policy Committee
summary: On 6 August 2025, the Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee voted to keep the policy repo rate unchanged at 5.50%. The decision followed its assessment of the evolving macroeconomic situation and the inflation outlook.
why: The policy rate is a key instrument used by the RBI to influence monetary and credit conditions. A pause indicates that the committee chose to hold the rate while assessing incoming economic data; it does not mean all lending rates remained unchanged.
impact: The decision applied to India's monetary-policy framework nationally. Mumbai is shown as the RBI's headquarters and institutional location, rather than as the geographic limit of the policy's effects.

title: Federal Reserve begins a new rate-cutting phase
entity: Federal Reserve; Federal Open Market Committee
summary: On 17 September 2025, the Federal Open Market Committee lowered the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 4.00%–4.25%. Further quarter-point cuts followed in October and December 2025.
why: The decisions marked a renewed easing phase after the Federal Reserve had held rates steady earlier in 2025. U.S. policy rates influence global borrowing costs, currency markets, capital flows and financial conditions.
impact: The policy decision was made in Washington, D.C., with effects transmitted through U.S. and international financial markets.

sources.label: Federal Reserve — Open Market Operations and FOMC rate history

title: United States enters its longest government-wide shutdown
entity: U.S. Congress; U.S. Federal Government
summary: A funding lapse began on 1 October 2025 after Congress did not enact the required appropriations or a continuing resolution. The government-wide shutdown lasted 42 full days and ended on 12 November 2025.
why: The shutdown interrupted or delayed parts of federal operations, affected federal workers and contractors, and created uncertainty around public services and economic data releases.
impact: The shutdown affected federal agencies and people across the United States. Washington, D.C. is shown as the seat of the federal government, not as the only place affected.

sources.label: Congressional Research Service — Federal Funding Gaps: A Brief Overview

title: Indian banks' gross NPA ratio reaches a multi-decadal low
entity: Reserve Bank of India
summary: The RBI's Report on Trend and Progress of Banking in India 2024–25 reported that scheduled commercial banks' gross non-performing asset ratio declined to 2.2% at end-March 2025, a multi-decadal low, and to 2.1% at end-September 2025.
why: The improvement reflected stronger asset quality across the banking system and was an important indicator of bank balance-sheet resilience. The ratio is a system-wide measure and should not be confused with the rupee amount of bad loans.
impact: The finding covers scheduled commercial banks across India. Mumbai is used as the RBI's institutional location.

sources.label: RBI — Report on Trend and Progress of Banking in India 2024–25, 29 December 2025

title: Stablecoins emerge as an FX hedge in parts of Africa
entity: African crypto-asset and stablecoin users; OECD
summary: The OECD's Africa Capital Markets Report 2026 documents emerging stablecoin and crypto-asset use cases across African jurisdictions. It notes that consumers and corporates in Zimbabwe have used crypto-assets and stablecoins as hedges against foreign-exchange risk and inflationary pressures.
why: The evidence points to a growing but uneven set of use cases, not widespread adoption by African corporates as a whole. Adoption, regulation and transaction patterns differ substantially between countries.
impact: The cited corporate FX-hedging use case is specifically documented in Zimbabwe. It should not be generalized to the entire African continent.

title: India presents the Union Budget for 2026–27
entity: Ministry of Finance; Government of India
summary: On 1 February 2026, the Union Finance Minister presented India's Union Budget for 2026–27 in Parliament. The budget set out the government's fiscal estimates, taxation proposals and spending priorities for the coming financial year.
why: The annual budget influences public expenditure, taxation, borrowing requirements and sectoral policy. Its proposals can affect households, businesses, investors and the government's financing needs, subject to legislative approval and implementation.
impact: The budget is a national fiscal policy statement. Its effects depend on the final enacted measures and subsequent implementation across states, sectors and public services.

title: RBI keeps the repo rate at 5.25%
entity: Reserve Bank of India; Monetary Policy Committee
summary: On 6 February 2026, the Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously to keep the policy repo rate unchanged at 5.25% and continue with a neutral stance.
why: The decision reflected the MPC's assessment of domestic and global economic conditions and its growth and inflation outlook. A policy-rate hold is a monetary-policy decision, not evidence that borrowing rates for every household or business remained unchanged.
impact: The decision applied nationally. Mumbai is used as the institutional map location for the RBI, not as a claim that the policy's effects were geographically limited to the city.

title: India retains its 4% inflation target through 2031
entity: Government of India; Reserve Bank of India
summary: On 25 March 2026, the Government of India, in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India, notified the continuation of the consumer-price inflation target at 4%, with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2 percentage points, for the five years beginning 1 April 2026.
why: The inflation target provides the framework for India's flexible inflation-targeting monetary policy regime. It gives the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee a continuing benchmark for assessing price stability while considering growth.
impact: The framework applies nationally and shapes the mandate against which monetary policy is assessed. It does not predetermine the repo rate or guarantee that inflation will remain within the tolerance band.

sources.label: RBI — Monetary Policy Report, April 2026

title: Indian rupee records a sharp structural adjustment against the US dollar
entity: Reserve Bank of India; Government of India
summary: A Government of India statement to Parliament reported that the rupee closed at ₹94.82 per U.S. dollar on 27 March 2026, representing a 9.9% depreciation during FY2025–26 up to that date.
why: The exchange-rate movement occurred amid global risk aversion, capital-flow pressures and geopolitical uncertainty. The rupee's movement was not unique among Asian currencies, several of which also weakened against the dollar.
impact: The exchange-rate movement affected India's foreign-exchange market and import costs. Mumbai is used as the RBI's institutional location.

entity: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
summary: On 7 April 2026, SEBI issued a circular providing relaxation from specified provisions of its master circular relating to non-compliance with minimum public shareholding requirements under the Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements framework.
why: Minimum public shareholding rules are intended to support public float and market liquidity. The circular adjusted the compliance framework for specified cases; it should not be described as a blanket removal of minimum public shareholding requirements.
impact: The regulatory circular applies to the relevant listed entities and market participants under SEBI's jurisdiction.
